title: Kiosk Checkout Row Context
lede: The idle dashboard is read by staff at the counter: each row must identify the booking, who holds it, how much custody is involved, and when it is due. The item manifest belongs one tap deeper in checkout details.

stats.n: Copy-only change; due-time pill and Return action remain in place
Holder identity plus singular/plural item count

sections.heading: Side by side
sections.note: Same iPad Air 11-inch simulator, same live kiosk fixture, same dashboard state. The clock/freshness stamp naturally advanced between captures; the checkout row structure and fixture records are otherwise unchanged.

pairs.title: Active checkout rows
pairs.sub: Look at the secondary line under each booking name.
pairs.beforeCap: The row spent its only small supporting line on a truncated item-name preview, which did not help staff identify the holder or the size of the custody.
pairs.afterCap: The row now answers who and how much at a glance: requester name plus item count. Tap the row for the actual manifest.

changes.h: The secondary line now carries operational context
changes.was: Item names were previewed under the booking title. With several items, the line became a truncated list and still omitted the person responsible for the checkout.
changes.now: The line reads `Requester · n item(s)`, with correct singular/plural grammar. The accessibility label also names the holder and count, while the detail drawer remains the complete item-manifest surface.

verification: 16 focused Vitest source-contract tests pass across the idle checkout list, sleep-mode removal, and iOS quality contracts.
WisconsinKiosk Xcode build and run succeeds on the iPad Air 11-inch (M4) simulator, iOS 26.5.
Runtime snapshot exposes `Kelsey Sharkey · 1 item`, `Maddy Pehler · 7 items`, and `AJ Harrison · 1 item`; the removed sleep control is absent.
notes: The due pills still use absolute weekday/date text even when a checkout is due today. A follow-up could use `Due today · 12:00 PM` or a short relative countdown for near deadlines.
The stat tiles are real filters, but the filter glyph is subtle. A follow-up could label the control group or make the active-list relationship explicit without adding another dashboard section.
No change was made to those two follow-ups in this slice; they need a deliberate copy/interaction decision rather than being bundled into the row subtitle fix.
